changed the sign of the boundary value and reversed the inequality

questions.stem: Hector used a tool called an auger to remove barley from a storage bin at a constant rate. The bin contained 19,600 bushels of barley when Hector began to use the auger. After 8 hours of using the auger, 13,216 bushels of barley remained in the bin. If the auger continues to remove barley at this rate, what is the total number of hours Hector will have been using the auger when 6,034 bushels of barley remain in the bin?
questions.rationale: The sentence gives 19,600 - 798u = 6,034, where u is the unknown, so u = 17.
reasons: found the extra hours after the first reading instead of the total
near-miss arithmetic slip
near-miss arithmetic slip

questions.stem: A rubber ball bounces upward one-half the height that it falls each time it hits the ground. If the ball was originally dropped from a distance of 26.0 feet above the ground, what was its maximum height above the ground, in feet, between the second and third time it hit the ground?
questions.rationale: Each bounce reaches one-half of the previous height, so after 2 bounces the height is 26.0/4 = 6.5 feet.

questions.stem: Which of the following expressions is equivalent to w² + 16w − 5 ?
questions.rationale: Half of 16 is 8, and (w + 8)² already carries 64, so −69 is what is left to reach −5.
reasons: halved the middle coefficient but changed its sign
halved the middle coefficient with the wrong sign and corrected the wrong way too
added the correction instead of subtracting it

questions.stem: In a group, 50% of the items are polished. Of all the polished items in the group, 60% are also hollow. What percentage of the items in the group are polished and hollow?
questions.rationale: 50% x 60% of the whole is 30%.
reasons: used the first percentage alone
added the percentages instead of taking a percent of a percent
divided one percentage by the other

questions.stem: One of the two equations in a linear system is 12x + 10y = 24. The system has no solution. Which of the following could be the other equation in the system?
questions.rationale: Dividing 12x + 10y = 24 by 2 gives 6x + 5y = 12, so an equation with the same left side and a different right side describes a parallel line and the system is empty.
reasons: swapping the coefficients and changing a sign changes the rate of change, so these lines still cross once
swapping the two coefficients changes the rate of change, so these lines still cross once
this is the given equation divided through by 2, so the two are the same line and every point on it solves both

questions.stem: The functions f and g are defined as f(x) = (1/2)x − 17 and g(x) = (1/2)x + 4. If the function h is defined as h(x) = f(x) + g(x), what is the x-coordinate of the x-intercept of the graph of y = h(x) in the xy-plane?
questions.rationale: h(x) = x − 13, which is zero at x = 13.

questions.stem: f(x) = ax² + 4x + c In the given quadratic function, a and c are constants. The graph of y = f(x) in the xy-plane is a parabola that opens upward and has a vertex at the point (h, k), where h and k are constants. I. c < 0 II. a ≥ 2 If k < 0 and f(−7) = f(5), which of the following must be true?
questions.rationale: f(−7) = f(5) puts the vertex at h = −1, so a = −4/(2 · −1) = 2; k < 0 only bounds c from above.
reasons: claims I and II, which the printed facts do not force
claims I only, which the printed facts do not force
claims Neither I nor II, which the printed facts do not force

y = x² + 2x − 18
y − 5x + 20 = 0
How many solutions are there to the system of equations above?
questions.rationale: Setting the two right-hand sides equal gives x² − 3x + 2 = 0, whose discriminant is 1, so the graphs share exactly two points.
reasons: read the sign of the discriminant the wrong way round, and concluded that the curve never meets the axis
multiplied the number of solutions of the quadratic by the two branches of the curve
counted the two square roots of a positive number as a single solution

questions.stem: A botanist recorded the species and the site of each of the 223 trees in a survey. If one of these trees is selected at random, what is the probability of selecting a tree at the south site, given that the tree is a birch or a willow?
questions.rationale: There are 132 birches and willows, and 62 of them are at the south site, so the probability is 31/66.
reasons: divided by all 223 trees instead of by the 132 birches and willows
used the number of trees at the south site over all 223 trees, ignoring the condition
divided by the number of trees at the south site instead of by the number of birches and willows — the conditional the other way round

choices: All adult patrons at the branch
All adult patrons in the county library system
latex: All adult patrons at the branch
All adult patrons in the county library system

read a sample that was not selected at random as if it had been, and generalized from it

questions.stem: A rectangular tile has an area of 200 square inches. A copy of the tile is made in which the length and width of the original tile are each decreased by 50%. What is the area, in square inches, of the copy?
questions.rationale: Each dimension is multiplied by 1/2, so the area is multiplied by (1/2)² = 1/4: 200 × 1/4 = 50.

questions.stem: In the xy-plane, point G is the center of a circle of radius 5, point U on the circle has coordinates (0, −5), and point V on the circle has coordinates (x, 5), where x is a constant. Which of the following could be the positive measure of angle UGV, in radians?
questions.rationale: V must be (0, 5), the far end of the diameter through U, so angle UGV is a half turn plus any whole number of full turns: π + 24π = 25π.
reasons: a half-integer multiple of π stops a quarter turn away, at (5, 0)
an even multiple of π is a whole number of full turns, which ends back at U
a half-integer multiple of π stops a quarter turn away, at (−5, 0)

y = x + 9
What is the solution (x, y) to the given system of equations?
questions.rationale: Putting 11 in place of x in y = x + 9 leaves one unknown, so the pair is (11, 20).
reasons: lost the sign when dividing to find x
wrote the two coordinates in the wrong order

questions.stem:
20x − 18y > −40
Which of the following inequalities is equivalent to the inequality above?
questions.rationale: Every term of 20x − 18y > −40 is a multiple of 2, and dividing a strict inequality by a positive number leaves it pointing the same way, so it is 10x − 9y > −20.
reasons: divided each term by its own coefficient instead of by the factor all three share
divided correctly but then exchanged the two coefficients
wrote the two terms the other way round and divided the constant by the first coefficient

questions.stem: A market researcher selected 250 people at random from a group of people who indicated that they liked a certain book. The 250 people were shown a movie based on the book and then asked whether they liked or disliked the movie. Of those surveyed, 90% said they liked the movie. Which of the following inferences can appropriately be drawn from this survey result?
choices: Most people who dislike this book will dislike this movie.
Most people who like this book will like this movie.
Most people who like this book will dislike this movie.
At least 90% of people who read books will like this movie.
latex: Most people who dislike this book will dislike this movie.
Most people who like this book will like this movie.
Most people who like this book will dislike this movie.
At least 90% of people who read books will like this movie.
questions.rationale: The people were selected at random from people who like this book, so only a claim about that group is licensed; 90% of one sample estimates the population rather than fixing it, so only “most” is supported.
reasons: swapped the group the sample came from for its complement, and the response with it
read the minority response of the sample as its majority response
generalized to a population the sample was never drawn from

reasons: took the square root of the sum of the legs instead of the sum of their squares

y = −27x + 32
Which table gives three values of x and their corresponding values of y for the given equation?
questions.rationale: Each input goes into y = −27x + 32 on its own: the coefficient of x multiplies the input, and the constant term is added afterwards, not once per row.
reasons: used the coefficient of x as the value at x = 0 and then added the constant term once for each row of the table
used the coefficient of x as the value at x = 0 and then multiplied it by each input
subtracted the constant term from the coefficient of x and used that as the slope

Which of the following systems of inequalities best represents this situation, where a is the number of azaleas that will be planted, and b is the number of boxwoods that will be planted?
questions.rationale: No more than 268 bushes in all is a + b ≤ 268, and at most twice as many azaleas as boxwoods is a ≤ 2b.
reasons: put the 2 on the wrong side of the second condition
read the cap as a total that has to be reached and put the 2 on the wrong side
read the cap as a total that has to be reached

did not take the square root of the coefficient of u²

wrote the two coordinates the wrong way round
lost the sign of the x-coordinate

questions.stem: Which of the following is equivalent to ¹⁰√(y² + 18y + 81), where y > 0?
questions.rationale: y² + 18y + 81 is (y + 9)², and a root of index 10 divides that exponent by 10.
reasons: used the root's index as the exponent instead of dividing by it
factored the trinomial but never took the root
wrote the exponent as 1 over the index and forgot the 2 the square contributes

questions.stem: The table shows the number of state parks in a certain state that contain camping facilities and bicycle paths. If one of these state parks is selected at random, what is the probability of selecting a state park that does not have camping facilities, given that the state park does not have bicycle paths?
questions.rationale: There are 36 state parks that do not have bicycle paths, and 16 of them do not have camping facilities, so the probability is 16/36.
reasons: divided by all 67 state parks instead of by the 36 state parks that do not have bicycle paths
divided by the number of state parks that do not have camping facilities instead of by the number of state parks that do not have bicycle paths — the conditional the other way round
used the number of state parks that do not have camping facilities over all 67 state parks, ignoring the condition

questions.stem: A customer's monthly electricity bill was $28.00. Due to a rate reduction, her monthly bill is now $22.40. To the nearest tenth of a percent, by what percent did the amount of the customer's electricity bill decrease?
questions.rationale: The change is 5.6, and 5.6/28 = 20%.
reasons: subtracted the two values and read the difference as the percent
divided the change by the new value instead of by the original
reported the new value as a percent of the old one instead of the change

questions.rationale: The condition is x ≤ 3y + 4, and with y = 2 the right side is 10, so the greatest value x can take is 10.

questions.stem: For groups of 29 or more people, a museum charges $13 per person for the first 29 people and $4 for each additional person. Which function f gives the total charge, in dollars, for a tour group with n people, where n ≥ 29?
questions.rationale: The first 29 cost 377 and each of the remaining n − 29 costs 4, so the total is f(n) = 4n + 261.
reasons: used the per-person price of the first block as the constant term
charged the whole first block again on top of every person
added the two prices into the rate and subtracted the block

questions.stem: The equation (z² + 8z − 9)/(z + 9) = pz + k is true for all z ≠ −9, where p and k are integers. What is the value of p + k ?
questions.rationale: z² + 8z − 9 is (z + 9)(z − 1), so dividing by z + 9 leaves z − 1.
reasons: took k from the divisor rather than from the quotient
reported k on its own
reported p on its own

questions.stem: A model estimates that at the end of each year from 1999 to 2003, the number of beetles in a population was 200% more than the number of beetles in the population at the end of the previous year. The model estimates that at the end of 2000, there were 90 beetles in the population. Which of the following equations represents this model, where n is the estimated number of beetles in the population t years after the end of 1999 and t ≤ 4?
questions.rationale: A rise of 200% multiplies by 3, so the count at the end of 1999 was 90/3 = 30.
reasons: used the later count and read the percent as the factor
used the count a year later as the starting count
read the percent as the factor itself

questions.stem: A botanist selected 125 seedlings at random from the seedlings in a greenhouse and randomly assigned them to two groups. One group was grown under a blue lamp for 3 weeks and the other under the usual lamp. The group grown under the blue lamp put on significantly more stem growth. Which of the following is the most appropriate conclusion from this study?
choices: The blue lamp causes an increase in stem growth for the seedlings in this greenhouse.
There is an association between the blue lamp and an increase in stem growth for the 125 seedlings in the study.
There is an association between the blue lamp and an increase in stem growth for all seedlings of this species.
The blue lamp causes an increase in stem growth for all seedlings of this species.
latex: The blue lamp causes an increase in stem growth for the seedlings in this greenhouse.
There is an association between the blue lamp and an increase in stem growth for the 125 seedlings in the study.
There is an association between the blue lamp and an increase in stem growth for all seedlings of this species.
The blue lamp causes an increase in stem growth for all seedlings of this species.
questions.rationale: The seedlings were randomly assigned, so the difference between the groups is a cause; they were selected at random from the seedlings in this greenhouse, so the conclusion reaches that group.
reasons: under-claimed twice over: random assignment earns a cause, and random selection earns the group the units came from
generalized past the seedlings in this greenhouse, the group the seedlings were selected from
generalized past the seedlings in this greenhouse, the group the seedlings were selected from

questions.topic_name: Sample Statistics and Margin of Error
questions.stem: The results of two random samples of votes for a proposition are shown above. The samples were selected from the same population, and the margins of error were calculated using the same method. Which of the following is the most appropriate reason that the margin of error for sample A is greater than the margin of error for sample B?
choices: Sample A had a smaller sample size.
Sample A had a lower percent of favorable responses.
Sample A was reported at a higher level of confidence.
Sample A had a smaller number of votes that could not be recorded.
latex: Sample A had a smaller sample size.
Sample A had a lower percent of favorable responses.
Sample A was reported at a higher level of confidence.
Sample A had a smaller number of votes that could not be recorded.
questions.rationale: The two margins were found the same way from the same population, so the only thing that can differ is the size of the sample. Sample A has the wider margin, so sample A is the smaller sample and sample B is the larger one.
reasons: read the margin off the statistic, when the stem fixes the method and leaves only the sample size free
reached for the confidence level, which does widen an interval but which the stem has already fixed
looked for the difference in the votes that were lost rather than in the size of the sample

questions.rationale: 206 of the 363 responses are on one side and 157 on the other, a difference of 49, and 49/363 of 200 rounds to 27.

questions.rationale: The cube's volume is 2.90³ = 24.389 cubic meters, and each cubic meter has a mass of 981 kilograms, so the mass multiplies: 981 × 24.389 = 23,926.
